o1.biggest_strength: It ranks the groups the way I would. The 46 to 90 day group goes first with no code, Monsoon Dark gets its own track, and ex-subscribers wait behind a delivery gate. Group sizes are netted for overlap, and the profit table is built on the holdout-adjusted contacted counts.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Monsoon Dark draft promises a match but never names it or uses a farm or roast placeholder. The profit estimate also covers only first returning orders plus a loose 12-month extension, and a few details are odd, such as the ₹535 per ex-subscriber figure and a break-even lift given only for group G6.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name the closest dark roast in the Monsoon Dark draft and put a farm in every draft. Give a break-even lift for every group, not just G6. Show the 12-month value explicitly. Trim a little so it sits clearly inside the word limit.

o2.biggest_strength: It is clean and easy to read. The drafts use farm and match placeholders. The delivery gate is sound, with a fix for each cancel reason. The profit maths checks out (₹557, ₹442, and a net of ₹8.5 lakh with low and high cases).
o2.biggest_mistake: It starts with the 91 to 180 day group and gives the 9,000 customers at 46 to 90 days only an always-on nudge, not a campaign. Those are the cheapest customers to win back. It also gives group C 10% off from the first message, leading with price to a cold group.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the 46 to 90 day group wave 1 with a reminder and no discount. Net the subscriber overlap out of group A. Add a break-even lift per group. Cover the Monsoon Dark buyers in the 91 to 180 band as a separate, sized track.

reason: Output 1 puts the cheap, at-risk 46 to 90 day customers first, gives Monsoon Dark and ex-subscribers their own tracks, and nets group sizes and profit properly. Output 2 is tidy and its drafts are good, but it misses the priority order I wanted and leans on a discount for the cold group.
